newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed after Oct posts new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed after Oct posts new high.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed after the October contract posted a fresh contract high. Rolling of longs and mixed ideas on cash markets made for uneven price movement, traders said.

October live cattle posted a high of 73.550 cents per lb early and then fell for a net loss before firming again late to end 0.025 lower at 73.325 cents. Other months ended 0.450 higher to 0.025 lower.
After an early surge higher on spillover support from higher pork complex futures linked to Friday's bullish USDA hog report, futures showed turned mixed.

October was pressured by position rolling and concern cash markets may not be as strong as expected. Packer cutout margins turned deeply red late last week which forced them to cut back on the kill, traders said.

However, prices firmed again late as many traders still expect fed prices to advance. Feedlot supplies remain tight and there is no reason currently for cattle feeders to reduce asking prices from $73 per cwt or higher, they said.
Deferreds also recoverd late after slipping at midday. Back months hold a large discount to current price levels in anticipation of increased fed numbers later, sources said.
Iowa Grain and Refco bought October at the close. Refco had spread long December/short October early along with Merrill Lynch, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, volatility was weak with some liquidation in October. There was light commercial selling in December 62 calls and Cargill Investor Services actively bought August 64 calls, pit sources added.

Lower corn futures kept feeder cattle futures supported despite late profit taking. Futures advanced to best levels in 1-1/2 week highs, basis October, as easing feed costs offset recent weakness in cash feeder cattle prices, traders said.

Demand was mixed and offset scale-up selling by ING late and selling by Stone Traders. ING was an early buyer along with Cargill Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man. Fimat Futures USA notably sold April, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.18 at $63.30 per cwt.
Feeder cattle closed 0.675 to 0.300 cent higher with October up 0.525 at 64.450 cents.
